contract: Pure all-or-nothing admission over a caller-held state with an injected now_ms: one admission takes cost tokens from a per-tenant and a per-principal token bucket (whole-interval integer refill capped at capacity, no refill when the clock goes back) and one in-flight slot from a global and a per-tenant fair-share delivery/backpressure bound, or takes nothing and returns the unchanged state with the first refusing bound in the order keys, slots, tenant_slots, tenant_rate, principal_rate and, for a rate bound, the exact milliseconds until a retry could pass; release frees exactly the two slots of a live ticket once. At most max_keys buckets of each kind and per-tenant Backpressure states; a full bucket whose tenant has no live ticket is dropped to make room, oldest last_ms first. Fixed error atoms; no queue, process, clock, telemetry or log.
limits: One caller-held state that the host serializes: no distributed or multi-node limit and no persistence across restarts (a restart starts full). No queue, waiting, weighted fairness or priority; Oban fair queuing stays consumer queue and partition configuration. Costs are the host's estimate.

The key cap fails closed with keys: a flood of new principals in one tenant can refuse new principals of other tenants once max_keys is reached, so set it above the expected active set. A dropped bucket that is created again starts its interval phase at that now_ms, so its next refill can come up to one interval later than if it had been kept.
Each call revalidates the whole state in time linear in its buckets and live tickets. Finite seeded scenarios and a reference-model trace, not a proof.

grounding.claim: Listed scenarios pass for config bounds and key shape, exact refill, retry_after and cap including a clock that goes back and times up to 2^63 - 1, the unchanged state on each of the five refusals and their order, global and per-tenant fair-share slots with exact and double release, idle-bucket eviction order and Backpressure state bounds, malformed texts, costs, times and forged states, and a seeded 10,000-step admit/release trace (seed {280, 644, 2026}) that agrees step by step with an independent reference model; the kept-tenant-token, last_ms-to-now and skipped-tenant-slot negative controls fail under temporary edits. Finite evidence, not a proof.
Relies on pinned Elixir integer arithmetic, map and term ordering semantics, not a local proof.

The host holds and serializes the state, passes a truthful now_ms and releases each admitted ticket when its work ends. Slot counts use delivery/backpressure through its public API, and its README-documented erased state is read only to check a state's counts.

telemetry.contract: Pure policy decision; it emits no telemetry or log, and errors are fixed atoms that never echo a tenant or principal.

config.contract: Construction-time options are exactly tenant_rate, principal_rate, max_in_flight, tenant_in_flight and max_keys, validated by new/1 with {:error, :config}; there is no hot update, and changed limits are a new state.

control.contract: The Piece owns no process or lifecycle to pause, drain, resume or stop.
